doc: Deterministic validation. A gate is a command, the tools it needs, and the conditions under which it applies. `mix harness.gates --lane <lane>` resolves the lane against the current change, runs what it can, and reports every gate as passed | failed | skipped | unavailable. `unavailable` is never folded into `passed`: a lane with an unavailable gate reports `partial`, and the work it guarded is unverified.

lanes.doc: Runs in under a minute. For an in-progress change, not for landing one.
The default before asking for review. Everything fast runs, plus the domain gates the change actually triggers.
Equivalent to `mix precommit` plus the quality tools. Before merging to develop.
Before main. Adds the independent security scanners, the documentation build and the CI job bodies as CI actually runs them.
T4/T5. Everything in release, plus conditions no command can check — which is why they are listed as manual gates with named holders.
Promoting any evolvable harness artifact. Stages are ordered and none may be skipped.
Onboarding or changing a data source.

A cloud worker's epic, before its ready handoff (WF-021). No new gate. `ci.local` asks the question CI asks: it runs CI's three job bodies, `mix test` with `claude` and `bwrap` hidden, because CI has neither. `harness.test` is the environment-dependent tests for the harness profile: it runs the harness suite unwrapped in the worker's VM, and applies only when the epic touches `.agents/` or `apps/noetic_harness/`. WF-021's `lane_paths` runs the lane over merge-base(origin/develop, HEAD)..HEAD minus `.agents/runs/` and `.agents/handoff/`, the path set merge-check reads.

gates.note: Weakening this flag to land work is a constitution violation, not a build tweak.

gates.name: tests for the apps this change touched
gates.note: Product apps need a migrated acme_test; the harness app needs nothing.

gates.name: the whole suite
gates.note: The root `test` alias migrates acme_test first. Tests tagged :qdrant need the vector store; excluding them is a partial run and is reported as one.

gates.command: mix do --app noetic_harness cmd mix test

gates.name: harness definitions are internally consistent
gates.note: Registry parses, ids unique, every referenced skill/tool/capability/role/gate resolves, every workflow graph is well formed, every agent composes a prompt.

gates.name: client type-checks and its own tests run
gates.command: mix do --app acme_web cmd mix assets.check
gates.note: esbuild only strips types. Without tsc --noEmit the client is unchecked, and it stayed unchecked long enough to hide two real defects.

gates.name: typeql-check
gates.command: for f in {{files}}; do case "$f" in *.tql) printf 'typeql-check %s\n' "$f"; typeql-check < "$f" || exit 1 ;; esac; done
gates.note: Mandatory for any TypeQL change. Unavailable means the change is UNCERTAIN, not DONE. typeql-check reads a query from its first argument or from stdin — it does not take file paths, so the command redirects each file in rather than listing them; the first version of this gate passed filenames and would have reported every .tql file as a parse error. It is not installed here: TypeDB ships it through apt and Homebrew only.

gates.name: documentation builds
gates.note: doc/ is the prose search index. A docs build failure hides every spec and ADR from search.

gates.name: the CI job bodies, locally
gates.note: CI does not watch claude/** branches. This is the only thing that asks the question CI asks.

gates.name: sobelow
gates.note: Scoped to apps/acme_web with --root, and that scope is the gate. Run from the umbrella root Sobelow prints “This does not appear to be a Phoenix application”, scans nothing and exits 0 — a gate that passes by scanning nothing is worse than no gate, and this one did for its first day. It is deliberately not run over the other four apps: Sobelow is a Phoenix scanner, and over a CLI that reads its own definition files it reports every File.read as directory traversal. Adding skips for those would be the weakening this note exists to prevent.

gates.name: shellcheck over the shell this repository runs
gates.command: for f in {{files}}; do case "$f" in bin/*|scripts/*|*.sh) printf 'shellcheck %s\n' "$f"; shellcheck -x -S warning -- "$f" || exit 1 ;; esac; done
gates.note: an earlier change. `noetic-harness hook` runs on every prompt in every session here and its stdout is spliced into the agent's context; `scripts/lib/toolchain.sh` is sourced by everything. None of it was linted. `-x` so a sourced file is followed rather than reported as unfollowable, and `-S warning` because the three `info` findings in this tree are all deliberate single-quoted strings -- a floor is a decision, and raising it to silence a real finding would be a different one. What this gate does NOT catch, stated because the bead that asked for it assumed otherwise: `mkdir -p "${log%/*}"` against a path with no slash is valid shell with a logic error, and shellcheck has no rule for it. What it does catch is the class that cost a release -- `${!var:-}` and `${BASH_SOURCE[0]}` in a file that says `#!/bin/sh` are SC3053, SC3028 and SC3054.
